description: Congressman Mark Pocan (WI-02), member of the House Appropriations and Foreign Affairs Committee, is seeking a highly motivated, detail-orientated, and energetic individual with experience in digital media strategy and video editing for a Digital Director / Press Secretary position. Daily tasks include managing and creating a steady stream of digital content for the member's social media platforms and website; video filming and editing; producing a weekly podcast; graphic design, and daily press clips. Additionally, the position will assist the Communications Director with managing in-district media relations; drafting releases and advisories, and organizing press events. The ideal candidate will be creative, have a strong proficiency in crafting digital content, experience coordinating with media, and be a detail-oriented team player able to handle multiple tasks at once. Excellent writing and strong organizational skills are essential, along with the ability to be a self-starter while working in a fast-paced environment. Capitol Hill experience is a plus but not required. A sense of humor is greatly appreciated, and the position reports to the Communications Director. This is not an entry-level position. Qualified candidates should submit a cover letter, resume, two writing samples, and an example of previous digital media or graphic design projects to WI02JobOpening@gmail.com with "Digital Director / Press Secretary" in the subject line. Job opening closes COB on Friday, August 21st. No phone calls, faxes, or drop-ins please. This office is an equal opportunity employer; we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin or citizenship status, sex, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, sexual orientation, age, disability, or military status.

description: The Field Representative/Caseworker monitors and updates the Member and District Director on district and local issues. This position acts as a liaison to federal, district, and local agencies for the member and constituents and answers casework correspondence and verbal communications with constituents.

Informs the Member and District Director on any important developments and current events impacting the district
Builds and maintains positive relationships with constituents, key community leaders, and other stakeholders
Tracks news stories and social media posts for the Member and colleagues, including the communications team
Attends events to serve as a representative for the Member, as determined by the District Director
Handles various community issues in accordance with office policies and procedures
Supports Office in executing public meetings and annual Congressional activities such as the Congressional Art Competition, Congressional App Competition, and other similar events
Organizes workload to prioritize tasks in accordance with varying deadlines and ensure work is completed in an efficient and effective manner
Understands differing perspectives and opinions to navigate conflicts and develop solutions effectively

Acts as the representative for the Member within their area of responsibility including answering casework correspondence, meeting with constituents, verbal communications with constituents, and serving as a liaison with federal, district, and local agencies

Maintains up-to-date files on all cases and categories of information of importance to the office
Meets attendance requirements as established by the office
Maintains a good working relationship with the Member, staff, and constituents

Works well under pressure and handles stress

Previous office experience is preferred
Previous experience working for a Member of Congress, elected official, or government agency preferred
Advanced proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, After Effects, Premiere Pro) and other design tools
Strong understanding of digital platforms and the role of design in social media, online engagement, and web communication
Experience with digital video production and editing
Ability to juggle multiple projects and work under tight deadlines in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment
Strong attention to detail and a keen eye for visual storytelling and design
Knowledge of the San Gabriel Valley media

Ability to exercise discretion and independent judgment in fulfillment of casework responsibilities
Knowledge of office policies, practices, and procedures
Knowledge of office computer applications
Proficiency in word processing
Must have a vehicle and driver's license in good standing

description: The Island County Community Liaison serves as Rep. Larsen's primary representative to communities on Whidbey and Camano islands. The liaison is responsible for engaging with constituents, businesses, organized labor, nonprofit organizations, federal agencies, tribal governments and federal, state and local officials throughout Island County. The position covers a broad portfolio of federal issues, including military and veterans' affairs, service academy nominations, federal grants, housing, transportation, agriculture, outdoor recreation, access to recreation and outdoor spaces, and other matters assigned by the District Director. The liaison is expected to build strong relationships with community stakeholders, develop a detailed understanding of local projects and policy concerns, and communicate those priorities to the Representative and office staff. The liaison will also help stakeholders understand federal policies, programs, and opportunities that affect Island County. The position is based in Representative Larsen's Everett, Washington office and reports directly to the District Director. District staff work closely with the Washington, D.C., office, and all staff report to the Member and Chief of Staff. This is a full-time position with federal benefits such as health care, the Federal Employees Retirement System, Student Loan Repayment Program, vacation/annual leave, paid sick and parental leave, and others.
responsibilities: Serve as an official representative for Rep. Larsen at meetings, forums and public events
Build and maintain relationships with constituents, businesses, labor, non-profit organizations, federal agencies, tribal and local government, and other stakeholders in Island County
Travel regularly throughout the district to monitor local issues, projects and activities
Work with Washington D.C.-based staff on federal policy development and help interpret federal policies for local stakeholders
Assist constituents and organizations in navigating federal agencies, grants and other federal resources
Plan and coordinate meetings, public events, site visits, and other district activities
qualifications: Strong knowledge of Island County and North West Washington
Experience conducting outreach with government officials, cultural communities, the business community, organized labor and local stakeholder groups
Strong understanding of veteran's issues, active duty and reserve issues, as well as military organizational structures and relevant terminology
Ability to exercise discretion and independent thinking while working as part of a team on sensitive projects and issues
Excellent written and verbal communication skills and comfort with public speaking
Flexibility to work evenings and occasional weekends
A valid driver's license, reliable access to a vehicle and the ability to travel regularly throughout Island County and the congressional district
Self-motivated, great at multi-tasking, strong interpersonal skills with a teamwork-oriented attitude, and a strong desire to help people
Detail oriented and organized
how_to_apply: Interested candidates should send a resume and cover letter to cameron.caldwell@mail.house.gov as a single PDF document with the subject line "Community Liaison Application [Your Name]". Applications will be considered on a rolling basis.

Coordinating Capitol tours, flag requests, and other constituent-facing administrative services.
Supporting the Director of Operation's scheduling program including tracking and processing meeting requests, maintaining scheduling correspondence, and coordinating calendar logistics.
Assisting with meeting preparation, briefing materials, daily schedule logistics, and last-minute scheduling changes.
Keeping the Member organized, prepared, and on schedule throughout the day.

Collaborating with the Chief of Staff and Director of Operations on scheduling strategy and office operations, including travel coordination, reimbursements, records management, stocking supplies, and administrative projects.
Supporting the DC Intern Program.
qualifications: Exceptional organizational skills and meticulous attention to detail.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.

A positive attitude, willingness to learn, and commitment to public service.
Demonstrated interest in scheduling, logistics, calendar management, and office operations.
District or New York ties are a plus but not required.

description: The Communications and Correspondence Assistant supports district-based efforts to communicate and liaise with stakeholders and key audiences in person and across platforms. The Communications and Correspondence Assistant manages the Congresswoman's district communications with constituents. They build out coordinated outreach and comms plans that leverage opportunities to highlight local leaders/networks in the district, increase commendations, convene and connect, create press and social media pop moments, maximize Office visibility, and build the opt-in list. The position is based in-district. Regular travel between Chicago and DuPage County will be required. The ideal candidate is a team player who can juggle multiple projects, deliver high-quality, professional work quickly under high pressure and with tight deadlines, develop and implement new ideas, take and implement feedback effectively, and stay organized. The position assumes flexible hours, including long hours, nights, and weekends, as needed.
responsibilities: Outreach and Field: Implement the Office's aligned comms and outreach plan and strategy, representing the Congresswoman in the field.
Digital Content Development: Support the Office's bilingual (SPAN/ENG) digital strategy and website maintenance in collaboration with the Communications Director.
District Press Support: Assist in the execution of the Office's media and public relations strategy for the Member.
Event Planning and Management: Support the execution of press conferences, tele-town halls, and other events in both Washington, D.C., and the District.
Administration: Coordinate across functions to advance strategic priorities.
Performs other duties as assigned.
qualifications: Experience: 1-2 years of experience in field or communications for elected officials, government agencies, non-profit organizations, or similar entities.
Fluency in Spanish is highly preferred.
Community Relations Skills: Strong ability to build relationships with a broad range of government and community stakeholders.
Exceptional Communication Skills: Strong writing, editing, and proofreading skills. Track record of action-oriented/persuasive writing yielding results.
Media Proficiency: Strong understanding of print, broadcast, and online media.
Digital Proficiency: Functional understanding of Canva, Adobe Pro, and other platforms for communication, design and engagement.

Team Player: Ability to build and maintain positive working relationships and to coordinate efforts to reduce silos. Willingness to accept direction and performance-based criticism in stride, adapt, and deliver.

Detail and Deadline-Oriented: Capable of producing high-quality communications materials quickly, under tight deadlines with limited support. Track record of exceptional planning and time management. Ability to work under pressure, and comfortable balancing multiple responsibilities at once.
Strategic Thinker: Politically savvy and skilled at navigating challenging situations with constituents, the press and staff.
